config.title: Polling Hook

intro.title: Polling Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `usePolling` that automatically fetches data from an API at regular intervals. You will learn how to use the `useState` and `useEffect` hooks to manage state and side effects in a functional component. The main technologies involved are React hooks, JavaScript's `setInterval` for timing, and the `fetch` API for data retrieval. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that can be integrated into any component to enable real-time data updates through polling.
intro.usecase: Polling hooks are essential for building real-time dashboards that display live data updates without requiring manual page refreshes. In financial trading platforms, polling hooks continuously fetch stock price changes to keep charts and portfolios current. E-commerce admin panels use polling to monitor order status changes and inventory levels as they happen. Live sports score trackers implement polling to update game statistics and scores in real-time for viewers.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook that manages polling intervals
Configure polling frequency and control mechanisms within the hook
Initialize state variables to track polling status and data
Integrate the polling hook with a component to fetch and display data
Manipulate polling behavior through user interactions
Bind the polling hook's return values to component rendering logic
Update component state based on polling results

steps.title: Create the usePolling custom hook function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'usePolling' that takes 'url' and 'interval' as parameters. The function should be empty for now (just return null).
steps.hint: Remember that custom hooks in React are just JavaScript functions. Start with 'function usePolling(url, interval) {}' or 'const usePolling = (url, interval) => {}'.

// Import React and the hooks needed for polling

// Create the usePolling custom hook function
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named usePolling is defined with url and interval parameters, returning null.
successCriteria: The usePolling function is created with two parameters (url and interval) and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a function named 'usePolling' that takes 'url' and 'interval' as parameters and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Remember to create a function named 'usePolling' with two parameters (url and interval) that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for data and loading status in the hook
steps.instruction: Inside your usePolling function, use useState to create two state variables: one named 'data' initialized to null, and another named 'loading' initialized to true.
steps.hint: Call useState twice: once for data and once for loading. Remember to destructure the array returned by useState.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePolling hook will have two state variables ready to track polled data and loading status.
successCriteria: The usePolling function contains two useState calls: one for 'data' initialized to null and one for 'loading' initialized to true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both state variables: 'data' initialized to null and 'loading' initialized to true using useState.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use useState to create 'data' and 'loading' state variables with the specified initial values.

steps.title: Create a ref to store the polling interval ID
steps.instruction: Inside the usePolling function, use the useRef hook to create a ref called intervalRef and initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Call useRef with null as the initial value and assign it to a variable named intervalRef.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a ref to hold a timer ID
const timerRef = useRef(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePolling hook now has an intervalRef variable created with useRef, ready to store the interval ID for polling.
successCriteria: intervalRef is declared using useRef and initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useRef and initializing it to null. Check the syntax: const intervalRef = useRef(null);
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a ref using the useRef hook and initialize it to null.

steps.title: Define the fetchData function inside the hook
steps.instruction: Inside the usePolling function, define an asynchronous function named fetchData. This function should take a url parameter, fetch data from that URL, and update the state accordingly.
steps.hint: Create an async function that uses fetch to get data from the provided URL. Remember to handle the response by converting it to JSON.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePolling hook now contains an async fetchData function that will be used to fetch data from a URL.
successCriteria: An async function named fetchData is defined inside usePolling, taking a url parameter and containing fetch logic.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure fetchData is an async function that takes a url parameter and contains fetch logic.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function isn't defined correctly. It should be an async function inside usePolling that takes a url parameter.

steps.title: Set up the polling effect with useEffect
steps.instruction: Inside the usePolling hook, add a useEffect hook that calls fetchData immediately and sets up an interval to call fetchData repeatedly every 2 seconds. Store the interval ID in intervalRef and clear it in the cleanup function.
steps.hint: The useEffect should run once on mount (empty dependency array). Use setInterval to call fetchData every 2000ms, store the returned ID in intervalRef.current, and return a cleanup function that clears the interval.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePolling hook now includes a useEffect that starts polling immediately and cleans up the interval when the component unmounts.
successCriteria: The useEffect hook is added with an empty dependency array, calls fetchData immediately, sets an interval to call fetchData every 2000ms, stores the interval ID in intervalRef.current, and returns a cleanup function that clears the interval.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your useEffect includes all required parts: immediate fetchData call, 2000ms interval, storing the ID in intervalRef, and cleanup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect setup is missing or incorrect. Remember to use useEffect with an empty dependency array, call fetchData immediately, set an interval, store the ID, and provide cleanup.

steps.title: Return the data and loading state from the hook
steps.instruction: At the end of the usePolling hook function, return an object containing the data and loading state values.
steps.hint: The hook should expose its internal state so components using it can access the fetched data and loading status.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePolling hook now returns an object with data and loading properties that can be destructured by components using this hook.
successCriteria: The usePolling hook returns an object containing data and loading state values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning an object with both data and loading properties from the hook.

steps.title: Render the polled data and loading state in JSX
steps.instruction: In the PollDisplay component's return statement, add JSX that conditionally shows a loading message when loading is true, and displays the polled data when loading is false.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to check the loading state. When true, render a loading message; when false, render the data value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PollDisplay component will display 'Loading...' while data is being fetched, and show the actual data once it's loaded.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
